preconditions.expression: q == int(q) and q >= 1 and q <= 300000
preconditions.description: The number of queries q is an integer between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(n == int(n) and n >= 1 and n <= 300000 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line) <= 300000])
preconditions.description: Each query's array length n is an integer between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(all(a_i == int(a_i) and a_i >= 1 and a_i <= n for a_i in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit())
preconditions.description: Each element a_i in the array is an integer between 1 and n inclusive, where n is the length of the array.

preconditions.expression: sum(int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line) <= 300000) <= 300000
preconditions.description: The sum of all array lengths n across all queries does not exceed 300,000.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '\n'.join(str(count) for count in [sum(1 for i in range(n) for j in range(i, n) if is_stack_exterminable(a[i:j+1])) for n, a in queries]) + '\n'
postconditions.description: For each query, stdout contains the count of stack exterminable subarrays in the array, where a subarray is stack exterminable if, after processing it with the given stack rules, the stack is empty.

postconditions.expression: all(count == int(count) and count >= 0 for count in [sum(1 for i in range(n) for j in range(i, n) if is_stack_exterminable(a[i:j+1])) for n, a in queries])
postconditions.description: Each count is a non-negative integer representing the number of stack exterminable subarrays in the corresponding query.
